description:
GTM Engineer

Remote (ET & CT time zones only – some travel required)

About Us

Clasp is a venture-backed, mission-driven startup transforming access to education and career pathways. We are revolutionizing the way employers attract and retain critical talent and the way colleges and universities support their students through education financing — all while tackling the student debt crisis. (Yep, we think BIG.) We like to think of ourselves as more than a fintech; we're a catalyst for economic mobility.

A Forbes Fintech 50 company, portfolio company of SHRM (Society of Human Resource Management — the world's largest HR professional society), and one of Business Insider's "43 Start-Ups to Bet Your Career On in 2025," Clasp is driven by our commitment to social impact and innovation.

Clasp runs two go-to-market motions on one platform:

Clasp Talent sells a workforce financing benefit to healthcare employers — a B2B motion with long cycles, multi-stakeholder committees, and named accounts.

Clasp Finance originates loans to students at partner schools — a high-volume consumer funnel measured in applications, approvals, conversion, and unit economics. The two feed each other, and almost nothing about how they're instrumented is the same.

We need someone to build the machinery underneath both.

Who We Need

Clasp is hiring a GTM Engineer. This role is the accountable owner of Clasp's HubSpot instance and the systems that surround it — funnel architecture, revenue operations, lifecycle automation, scoring, routing, and reporting across both motions. What makes this an engineering role rather than an administrative one is the approach: you'd rather build a system that removes a manual process than run the manual process well, and you reach for an API or an automation before accepting that something has to be done by hand.

We're looking for the first hire in this seat. There's real mess to clean up and real leverage on the other side of it.

What You'll Do

HubSpot Ownership

  • Own the HubSpot instance end to end across portals: object model, lifecycle stages, properties, associations, pipelines, workflows, forms, integrations, and the marketing contact economics that determine what we pay.

  • Do the unglamorous work well — reconcile duplicate records, retire zombie workflows, audit which installed apps are quietly mutating data, keep consent and deliverability clean.

  • Know precisely why our contact tier and seat count are what they are, and be able to defend both at renewal.

Revenue Operations

  • Define funnel stages and GTM metrics that mean the same thing in every system, for two motions that don't naturally share a vocabulary.

  • Enforce pipeline and data hygiene through automation rather than by nagging reps.

  • Implement territory, segmentation, and ICP logic in the CRM instead of leaving it in a deck; own routing, SLAs, and lifecycle transitions.

  • Build lead and account scoring you can explain, and the quota and comp tracking infrastructure behind plan attainment.

Pipeline Systems & Growth Engineering

  • Build enrichment and data waterfalls, signal-based plays wired from public and product data, and automated research and personalization at the top of funnel.

  • Build lifecycle campaigns that fire on behavior rather than on a calendar.

  • Instrument the student funnel end to end so we can see where applicants stall and act on it inside a week.

  • Build and maintain landing pages, HubSpot CMS modules, and forms that support campaigns without a queue forming behind you.

Integrations & Data Flow

  • Build and maintain API, webhook, and OAuth integrations between HubSpot, our product, and third-party services.

  • Design dependable data flows with validation, observability, consent handling, access controls, and clear failure recovery.

  • Partner with our data team so HubSpot data lands clean and reportable in Snowflake and is trustworthy enough for the AI analytics agents our teams query in Slack.

Automation & AI

  • Identify where AI meaningfully removes work from the revenue org, and build it: enrichment and research agents, deal-desk assistants, self-serve reporting that doesn't route through a person.

  • Work within our existing patterns for production automation — scoped credentials, audit trails, kill switches. Our thesis is connective tissue, not foundation models.

  • Use AI-assisted development yourself where it improves quality and speed, with judgment about where it doesn't.

Change Management

  • Plan and land material changes to systems people are actively selling on — pipeline restructures, property migrations, workflow deprecations, new required fields — without breaking historical reporting or the team's trust.

  • Communicate changes before they ship, bring reps and CSMs along, and leave no quiet breakage behind.

  • Maintain a defensible record of what changed, when, why, and who approved it.

Stakeholder Management

  • Work with Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Finance, Data, and Engineering to translate business goals into working systems.

  • Explain technical tradeoffs, options, and risks clearly to non-technical stakeholders.

  • Manage expectations and say no to some of what you're asked for, with a reason people accept.

Delivery

  • Own work from discovery and design through implementation, testing, launch, and post-launch support.

  • Break work into clear milestones, communicate progress and risk honestly, and ship reliable increments on schedule.

  • Prioritize ruthlessly. There will be more demand here than capacity, permanently.

Enablement & Documentation

  • Document system architecture, CRM configuration, integration behavior, and operational runbooks for both technical and business audiences.

  • Train and support internal teams so they can confidently use, maintain, and troubleshoot what you deliver.

  • Build so that you are not the single point of failure. Nothing you own should be a black box, and we'd like to move parts of the stack toward version control over time — you'd help us decide where that's worth it and where it's overkill.

Performance & Conversion Optimization

  • Measure and improve conversion across both funnels; find the bottlenecks, including the ones inside our own workflows.

  • Use analytics instrumentation, monitoring, and production diagnostics to catch regressions before a rep or an applicant does.

  • Quantify the impact of what you build, and be honest about what didn't work.

What You'll Need

  • Bachelor's degree in a relevant field, or equivalent practical experience. We weight the work heavily over the credential.

  • 5+ years in revenue operations, marketing operations, GTM engineering, or an analytics role embedded in revenue, including 2+ years hands-on in HubSpot.

  • Experience building revenue infrastructure where little existed before.

  • Experience in a regulated industry — financial services, healthcare, insurance, or similar — where consumer data, consent, retention, and access controls have real rules attached, and where you treated those as design constraints rather than obstacles.

  • A track record of landing material CRM changes on a live revenue team without breaking their reporting.

  • Deep, hands-on HubSpot: custom objects and properties, workflows and custom code actions, forms, CMS modules, the CRM and Marketing APIs, association complexity, marketing contact economics. You've fixed an instance someone else broke.

  • SQL fluency and comfort reasoning about data models, not just running reports.

  • Working knowledge of REST APIs, OAuth, webhooks, data mapping, and reliable synchronization between systems — including what happens when a sync fails.

  • Enough scripting ability to automate rather than repeat yourself. We care more about how quickly you pick things up than what you already know; if there are gaps here, you'll close them on this team and we'll help.

  • Warehouse and BI exposure (Snowflake, dbt, or equivalent) is a strong plus.

  • Applied LLM tooling for enrichment, scoring, research, or GTM analytics, with a real view on where it works and where it doesn't, is a strong plus.

Nice to Have

  • Lending, fintech, or another high-volume consumer funnel.

  • Consumer funnel work and enterprise B2B pipeline work — both is rare and unusually valuable here.

  • Multi-product or multi-motion companies where one revenue vocabulary didn't fit the whole business.

What We Give in Return

  • Competitive cash and equity compensation.

  • Health benefits, including medical, dental, and vision coverage.

  • Student loan repayment benefits.

  • 401(k) + Match.

  • Flexible PTO.

  • Opportunities to grow with a fast-moving, mission-driven team.

     

Salary

The salary range for this position is competitive and will be commensurate with the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and industry knowledge, ranging between $155,000 to $185,000 annually. In addition to the base salary, we offer an attractive equity component as part of our compensation package, providing an opportunity for eligible employees to share in the success and growth of our company. We are committed to offering competitive compensation and benefits packages to attract and retain top talent.

Work authorization
This role is not eligible for immigration sponsorship, now or in the future. Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States for any employer.

How we use AI in hiring
Clasp uses AI-assisted tools in parts of our hiring process, such as AI notetakers transcribing or summarizing interviews, scheduling, and supporting evaluation in technical assessments. Humans review applications and make every hiring decision. AI tools don't make final decisions about any candidate. You're welcome to use AI to research Clasp and prepare, but during live interviews and assessments we want to hear your own thinking, so please don't use AI tools that generate or feed you responses in real time. If you'd like to be evaluated without AI tools, need an accommodation, or have questions about how we use these tools, email recruiting@clasp.com and we'll arrange another process where we can.

Equal opportunity
Clasp is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We don't discriminate based on race, color, religion, creed, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, and related conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, veteran or military status, citizenship status (except as required by law), or any other status protected by federal, state, or local law. Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered in line with applicable fair chance laws. If you need a reasonable accommodation during the hiring process, email recruiting@clasp.com.
